title: Pick up the dog's ball with the ball launcher
instruction: Pick the dog's ball up with the launcher without touching the ball, and hold it up off the mat.
context: Dog owners use ball launchers to pick up a wet ball without touching it; the maker sells it for hands-free pickup. The ball is a loose sphere, so it rolls away from a cup pushed at it from the side and squirts out from under a lip pressed off-centre. Unlike a reacher-grabber, the cup has no jaws to close: the catch only happens if a centred downward press on a ball that rolls away pushes the lips past its middle. The robot has to manage a 0.36 m tool held by its shaft.
setup: Station table, world frame: x away from the arms, y to the robot's left, z up; heights are above the mat top (table + 6 mm). Green outdoor mat, 0.30 x 0.60 m x 6 mm, fixed, covering x 0.10-0.40 m, y -0.20-0.40 m. Brown edging board along its far edge: 18 mm thick, 0.60 m long, its inner face at x 0.400 m, its top 15 mm above the mat. Ball: orange rubber dog ball, 50.8 mm diameter (Chuckit! small, 2 in), 45 g, resting on the mat. Ball launcher (Chuckit! Sport 14S size): 0.36 m long, 141 g, lime plastic with a blue handle. It lies cup-down with its shaft along +y: cup centre at (0.160, 0.000) m, 10.5 mm above the mat, handle end at y 0.336 m. Cup: inner radius 26.5 mm, 3 mm wall; a back plate 26.5 mm above the cup centre; side walls 40 mm long at 26.5-29.5 mm either side, reaching down to the cup centre and no lower. Two lips, one at the tip end and one at the shaft end of the cup, are 28 mm wide, 3 mm thick plates hinged at the back rim 28 mm either side of the cup centre. Each ends in a tooth 6.5-10.5 mm below the cup centre that reaches 3.5 mm inwards, so the tooth edges are 23.0 mm from the cup axis against the ball's 25.4 mm radius. A lip opens outwards against a 2.0 N m/rad spring (0 to 0.5 rad). Shaft: 300 x 14 x 10 mm, its centre line 16 mm above the cup centre, from 36 to 336 mm behind the cup centre; handle block 70 x 26 x 31.5 mm at 265-335 mm, resting on the mat. Lot A: ball centre at (0.3746, 0.040) m, touching the edging board. Lot B: ball centre at (0.270, 0.020) m in the open. The launcher is the same in both. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Per trial. 1.0: the ball is seated in the launcher's cup and lifted, and stays within 2 mm of where it was when the hold began, for 2 s in a row (world frame). 0.5: the ball is seated in the cup at the end of the trial (on the mat or lifted). Otherwise 0. Seated: in the launcher's own frame the ball centre is within 4 mm of the cup axis along the shaft, within 6 mm across it, and 1.1 +/- 3 mm above the cup centre (against the back), with both lips back within 0.12 rad of closed, so both teeth are under the ball. Lifted: the ball's bottom is at least 60 mm above the mat. Whole trial, any violation scores 0: no gripper or fingertip surface ever comes within 5 mm of the ball (that counts as touching it); the ball's centre never leaves the mat's area (x 0.10-0.40 m, y -0.20-0.40 m) or drops more than 5 mm below its resting height. Unknown or invalid hand or object state at any step scores 0. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 600 control steps (30 s at 20 Hz) per trial; 2 trials (lots A and B).
fidelity: True size from the maker's scaled photo and listing (14 in, 2 in ball, 0.31 lb). Curved cup shell and lips are built from boxes; lips are rigid plates on sprung hinges. Lip stiffness (2.0 N m/rad), ball mass (45 g) and frictions are estimates. The mat's rolling resistance is stood in for by ball angular damping (4/s, uncalibrated). The shaft is straight. Two layouts stop one fixed replay, not a memorised pair.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B; 600-step limit in both). Demo: 1.0 in each of lots A and B. object_jitter=0, --epochs 2.
reset_notes: 1. Take the ball out of the cup by hand. 2. Lay the launcher cup-down on the mat with its shaft along +y: cup centre at (0.160, 0.000) m, handle towards the robot's left, resting on its two lip teeth and its handle. 3. Lot A: set the ball touching the edging board with its centre at (0.3746, 0.040) m. Lot B: set the ball at (0.270, 0.020) m. 4. Check that the ball does not roll and that both lips hang closed.
